status_note: NOT FROZEN. This file is a preregistration DRAFT written before any fit of this experiment exists. It carries no protocol_hash on purpose: a hash here would look like a freeze. Freezing is a separate, later commit that (i) renames this to em_convergence_sensitivity_20260905_protocol.json, (ii) adds protocol_hash, and (iii) happens only after the replication gate passes and after a human authorises production under CLAUDE.md section 6.
research_question: Does relaxing the fixed 8-iteration optimization budget materially change the selected-K pattern under the otherwise frozen clean-generator protocol?
what_this_is_not: not a proof or a test of K-selection consistency
not additional evidence for the true-K identifiability theory
not a proposal of a new selection criterion
not tuning aimed at making K=5 win

baseline.role: paired control arm; NOT re-run, NOT modified, NOT regenerated

held_fixed_from_baseline.selection_aggregation: unweighted mean over the two starts
held_fixed_from_baseline.model_seed_formula: MODEL_SEED_BASE + k_true*100000 + n*1000 + replicate*100 + k_est*10 + start
held_fixed_from_baseline.seed_bases_source: read from the baseline protocol.json, never retyped

the_only_thing_that_changes: the optimization budget: num_iter 8 -> a single run of 40 iterations per fit, with the criteria evaluated at preregistered checkpoints

scope.replicate_selection: ALL 8 replicates of every scoped cell; no subsetting, so no cherry-picking rule is needed

excluded.n_50: n=75 already shows the strongest under-selection in the baseline (S1 exact 0/8 versus 2/8 at n=50), so n=50 is not the extreme case and adds a fourth point without adding a contrast. Recorded here BEFORE any new fit exists.
excluded.k_true_1: confounded three ways in the baseline (floor of the candidate set, under-selection dominance, heaviest-tailed signal); it cannot discriminate between the two explanations
excluded.k_true_3: only 4 replicates per cell; the budget contrast would rest on half the sample of K_TRUE=5

scope.scope_is_result_informed_note: The choice of K_TRUE=5 and of these three n IS informed by the baseline result. This is unavoidable -- the question is about that observed under-selection -- but it means this experiment is a targeted follow-up, not an independent test. The rule is fixed here, before any new data exists, and no outcome may change it.

optimization_budget.rationale: One run of 40 iterations costs 40 iterations; running 8/12/16/24/32/40 separately costs 132. The prefix property that makes the two equivalent is asserted in tools/research_audit/test_em_budget_nesting.py (N1) and is verified against the archive by the replication gate.
optimization_budget.adaptive_stopping_note: There is NO adaptive stopping rule. Every candidate K receives exactly the same number of iterations, so a stopping rule cannot favour or disfavour any K. Convergence is measured and reported, never used to stop, and never used to select K.

convergence_diagnostics.budget_stable_at_tau: max param_rel_change over the last 4 iterations before the checkpoint < tau
convergence_diagnostics.tau_ladder_note: ALL THREE are reported. No single tau is designated 'the' convergence threshold, because choosing one after seeing the results is exactly the move this preregistration exists to prevent.
convergence_diagnostics.monte_carlo_floor_caveat: L=5 latent draws are redrawn every iteration, so param_rel_change does not decay to zero even at a fixed point. Any tau is therefore a statement about the size of the Monte-Carlo jitter as much as about convergence, and the jitter may itself depend on K. This is an accepted, declared limitation of this design, not something it resolves.
convergence_diagnostics.q_trajectory: recorded via the existing mstep_q_diagnostic hook (q_before / q_after around each M-step, on the same Z_samples)
convergence_diagnostics.q_trajectory_caveat: q_before/q_after share one E-step's draws, so the within-iteration difference is a valid M-step monotonicity check, but the sequence ACROSS iterations is not a monotone objective and must not be read as one.

primary_outcomes.name: selected K by budget
primary_outcomes.definition: selected K per (criterion, n, replicate) at each checkpoint, with the frozen selector unchanged
primary_outcomes.comparison: checkpoint 8 versus checkpoint 40, paired within replicate

primary_outcomes.name: per-candidate-K score gain from extra iterations
primary_outcomes.definition: delta_K = mean S1 held-out score at checkpoint 40 minus at checkpoint 8, for each candidate K
primary_outcomes.comparison: is delta_K increasing in K? Reported as the full table plus the Spearman correlation between K and delta_K within each n. Descriptive only: 7 points, no inferential claim, no p-value threshold.
primary_outcomes.note: This is the outcome that most directly separates the two explanations.

secondary_outcomes: exact / under / over counts by budget, with over-selection cells named individually
winning margin (best minus runner-up in selector space) by budget
budget_stable_at_tau rates by candidate K and by n
Q_strict and S2 trajectories by candidate K
cumulative runtime by checkpoint, candidate K and n
S2 and S3 versions of P1 and P2

A.pattern: delta_K increases with K and selected K moves toward K_TRUE at longer budgets
A.reading: evidence for fixed-budget optimization confounding; the baseline under-selection may NOT be attributed to the criteria
A.forbidden: must not be reported as 'the criteria work after all' -- it says the 8-iteration result was budget-limited, nothing about consistency

B.pattern: objective and convergence diagnostics improve but selected K is essentially unchanged
B.reading: under-selection is not explained by the 8-iteration truncation alone
B.forbidden: must NOT be reported as proof that the cause is the criterion; L, the MC floor and the initialisation remain uncontrolled

C.pattern: high-K fits are already budget-stable at iteration 8
C.reading: the F-02 optimization explanation is weakened for this setting
C.forbidden: must not be generalised beyond K_TRUE=5 and these three n

D.pattern: longer optimization destabilises selection or increases over-selection
D.reading: optimization and criterion interact; report as an interaction, not as degradation
D.forbidden: the word 'improvement' must not be used in any direction

interpretation_matrix.meta: All four are scientific results. K=5 failing to win more often is NOT a failed experiment, and no outcome may trigger a protocol change, a re-run, a seed change or an added arm.

pilot.name: replication gate
pilot.purpose: prove that the new instrumented runner reproduces the archived baseline exactly at checkpoint 8, so that the paired comparison is a comparison of budgets and not of code paths
pilot.scope: K_TRUE=5, n=75, replicate 1, all 7 candidate K, both starts
pilot.pass_condition: for all 14 fits, heldout_mean_log_score, q_strict, s2_q_based, s3_plugin_conditional and num_params are EXACTLY equal (bit-identical float repr) to the corresponding rows of the archived fit_results.csv, and train/test mask hashes match mask provenance
pilot.on_fail: BLOCKER. Production is not authorised. Do not adjust tolerances, do not switch to approximate comparison, do not proceed with an unpaired design.
pilot.freeze_rule: The protocol is hashed and frozen BEFORE the pilot runs. The pilot may only return PASS or FAIL; it may not change any protocol field. If a field would have to change, the protocol is re-frozen as a new version and the pilot is re-run in full.

runtime_estimate.projection_method: linear in iteration count; conservative because each fit also pays a fixed end-of-run cost that does not scale
runtime_estimate.checkpoint_overhead_note: six checkpoint evaluations per fit instead of one final evaluation; each costs one Q_strict, one held-out score and one S3 pass, all deterministic. Budget an additional allowance rather than assuming it is free.
runtime_estimate.abort_threshold: if elapsed time exceeds 2x the projection, stop and write failure.json; do not resume

f08_resolution.problem: em_runner resets nan_count at the top of every retry and breaks on the first clean attempt, so an internal NaN restart is invisible in the returned counters
f08_resolution.fix: the new runner owns its own iteration loop and appends {attempt, iteration, kind} to retry_events for every NaN event and every restart, and reports attempts_used; a value greater than 1 is a PAIRING FAILURE for that fit, recorded as such and never silently absorbed

not_recorded_and_why.gradient_norm: the E-step Newton solve does not return its gradient; exposing it would change the model classes, which are shared with the historical lineage
not_recorded_and_why.held_out_score_per_iteration: recorded only at checkpoints, deliberately -- a per-iteration held-out trace invites using it as a stopping signal, which would be leakage

prohibitions: no re-run of the archived 896-fit baseline
no modification, regeneration or deletion of any archived artifact
no retry, replacement, resume, seed rescue or tolerance relaxation
no protocol or criterion change after any fit of this experiment exists
no promotion of lineage E results to manuscript evidence (Human Gate)

claim_boundary.lineage: E (experimental prototype); EXPERIMENT_REGISTRY records 原稿採用 ✗
claim_boundary.scope: one synthetic setting, K_TRUE=5, three n, Poisson-X / Bernoulli-Y, one signal level
does_not_establish: identifiability for Bernoulli-Y (U2) or non-nesting for Bernoulli-Y (U5)
that the fixed point reached at 40 iterations is the MLE
